newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower ahead of legal decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower ahead of legal decision.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Sunday in mixed trading as investors waited to see if the attorney-general would charge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scadal, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.64 percent, or 1.59 points, to 247.68 on an all-share turnover of 95 million shekels against 99 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.69 percent lower at 257.61.
An official announcement by the attorney-general on whether Netanyahu will be indicted will be announced later on Sunday after the end of the trading day.

Last week police recommended the prime minister and three officials be charged with fraud and breach of trust over the short-lived appointment of political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney-general in January.
On Monday and Tuesday the stock exchange will remain closed for the Jewish holiday of Passover.

"The market is on hold today as investors wait for the attorney-general's decision. Despite that, the market continues to show strength and it remained mixed and balanced today," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments and Securities.

"If it was not for Teva the market would have closed almost unchanged. Overall it seems that the market is very quiet but as long as there is uncertainty the market will remain very nervous," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the second most active share, fell 3.25 percent to 17,859 agorot on volume of 8.4 million shekel. Traders said Teva fell after its issue traded on Nasdaq plunged 5.0 percent.
"Political uncertainty is not good for the market and if we are going to face a political turmoil the market will remain very nervous," Hoffman said.
Koor Industries fell 1.75 percent to 30,113. Koor subidiary Telrad Holdings announced on Sunday that it had purchased about four million dollars worth of shares in Koor.
The most active share was Israel Discount Bank, which fell 0.75 percent to 337 agorot on volume of 9.7 million shekels.
Clal Industries, the third most active share, lost 2.0 percent to 1,581 agorot on turnover of 5.5 million shekels.
